Maths Path · Ages 8 to 9

Class 4 maths

Bigger numbers, area, symmetry and budgets. Go in order. Pass each check to open the next chapter.

0 of 9 passed

Class 4 chapters in order

  1. 1

    Bigger numbers, factors and Roman numerals

    Use place value beyond four digits and investigate exact groups.

    • I can build and compare larger numbers.
    • I can find factors and multiples.
    • I can read and use Roman numerals.
    Not started
  2. 2

    Calculate and solve step by step

    Choose operations, use written methods and check missing information.

    • I can multiply and divide using models.
    • I can interpret a remainder.
    • I can solve a linked story or missing digit.
    Not started
  3. 3

    Compare and use fractions

    Keep track of the whole while matching parts and solving changes.

    • I can show equal fractions.
    • I can find a fraction of an amount.
    • I can find what is left after fraction changes.
    Not started
  4. 4

    Perimeter, area and symmetry

    Separate the outside boundary from the space inside a shape.

    • I can find a perimeter or missing side.
    • I can find area using square units.
    • I can complete a reflection or folded solid.
    Not started
  5. 5

    Measure and convert units

    Read the scale and convert length, mass or capacity before calculating.

    • I can measure from a non-zero mark.
    • I can combine or share mixed units.
    • I can use balances and temperature scales.
    Not started
  6. 6

    Timetables, dates and clock errors

    Use intervals and distinguish the clock reading from the true time.

    • I can find a missing time interval.
    • I can use a timetable or calendar.
    • I can correct a fast or slow clock.
    Not started
  7. 7

    Bills, budgets and rupees with paise

    Keep rupees and paise lined up while comparing real shopping choices.

    • I can total a bill and find change.
    • I can compare equal amounts in packs.
    • I can choose within a budget.
    Not started
  8. 8

    Read scaled charts and compare results

    Use axes, half-symbol keys and totals across displays.

    • I can use a non-unit chart scale.
    • I can read half a pictograph symbol.
    • I can compare and update survey data.
    Not started
  9. 9

    Codes, turns and hidden pictures

    Explain each code, picture or ordering rule before selecting an answer.

    • I can use codes and alphabet order.
    • I can follow turns and ranking clues.
    • I can find a hidden figure or picture rule.
    • I can list possible pairs without missing any.
    Not started

Olympiad-style paper
